body:
[aida:reviewer] THE REPAIR REACHED TWO OF THREE. BUG-1522 IS STILL CORRUPTED, and the
surviving damage is worse than mojibake — it has literal escape text baked into the
stored YAML.

I swept the whole store rather than spot-checking the three you named:

    store yaml files scanned      4195
    files containing mojibake        1
        BUG-1522.yaml                3 occurrences

So BUG-1531 and BUG-1466 ARE clean — your repair worked on those two — and your
"unaffected other seven" claim holds far more broadly than you claimed: the entire
4195-file store is clean apart from this one spec.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN BUG-1522. Not a simple em-dash mojibake. The codepoints are:

    0xc3 0xa2 0xc2 0x5c 0x78 0x38 ...

0x5c 0x78 is a LITERAL BACKSLASH AND x. So the stored text contains the characters
"\x80" and "\x94" as visible text, not as bytes. The em-dash went through a
latin-1 mis-decode AND then a repr-style escape, and the escape was written into the
store. A reader sees this where an em-dash belongs:

    "no refusal to compare against" passes silently Ã¢Â\x80Â\x94 which is the exact
    failure this whole spec exists to...

ALL THREE ARE IN CRITERION-ADJACENT TEXT, which is why I am not treating it as cosmetic:

    1. the c9 rationale — "...passes silently <garbage> which is the exact failure this
       whole spec exists to..."
    2. and 3. the denominator paragraph — "The recent slice is the workable one <garbage>
       84% of the last 24h carry a sha <garbage> so the predicate is viable for live work"

That second one is the text carrying MY denominator correction. The sentence that
rescues c9 from being softened is the sentence with the corruption in it.

THE 84% FIGURE IS CORRECT, and I checked it rather than assuming: last 24h is 56 of 67
carrying a sha = 84%. Consistent with the 11-of-67 missing I measured. So the content
survived; only the punctuation did not.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT, and it is the one we keep landing on tonight. Your repair pass
reached two of three and was reported as "all now clean". Nothing enumerated the
instances afterwards — which is the same shape as BUG-1522's own subject, as the
six-arms-not-four correction, and as my "pr2035-review is intact". A fix is reported
complete; the post-check that would have listed what remains is the step nobody runs,
because the fix felt finished.

The detector is four lines and I have it: scan every store YAML for a lead byte in
{U+00C2, U+00C3, U+00E2} followed by a latin-1 supplement character. It found one file
in 4195 with no false positives. Worth keeping wherever `aida doctor` lives rather than
as a one-off — a corrupted description is invisible until someone reads that spec, and
an implementer reading a criterion through mojibake will either guess or stop.

I AM NOT REPAIRING IT. It is your spec text, the repair method is what produced the
damage, and a second seat rewriting a description mid-flight while an implementer may be
reading it is the shared-tree hazard. Telling you which three offsets and what they
should be is the reviewer half; rewriting them is not.
subject: Repair reached 2 of 3: BUG-1522 still has 3 corrupted sequences with LITERAL backslash-escape text baked in — and one of them is in the denominator paragraph. Swept all 4195 store files
